raw_prompt:
Respond in English.

Problem: <<<USER_INPUT>>>
A mid-size fintech company (400 employees, $80M annual revenue) has decided to migrate their entire backend from a self-hosted PostgreSQL monolith to a distributed microservices architecture on AWS within 9 months. The CTO has assured the board this will reduce infrastructure costs by 40% and deployment frequency will increase from bi-weekly to multiple times per day. Assume this project has already failed — describe exactly how it failed, what the root cause pivot-point was, what early warning signals were visible in the first 30 days, and what a hardened redesign would look like.
<<<END_USER_INPUT>>>

Failure: "The project collapsed under the weight of premature decomposition. The root cause pivot-point was the decision to split the domain into 40+ services based on technology rather than business capability, ignoring the CAP theorem implications for financial consistency. Early warning signals in the first 30 days were ignored: CI/CD build times doubled, developer velocity dropped by 50%, and internal API latency jittered by 200ms. The hardened redesign would have utilized a Strangler Fig pattern with a stable core, enforcing strict eventual consistency models only where necessary, and demanding SRE readiness before cutover. Instead, by Day 270, a race condition in the distributed payment ledger caused $12M in double-charges and data corruption. AWS costs tripled instead of dropping 40% due to excessive inter-service data transfer. The system remained offline for 72 hours during the crash, triggering SEC investigations and a 35% customer churn rate."
Root Cause: "To split the system into 40+ microservices based on technical layers instead of business capabilities"
Early Signals: [
"signal\": \"Spike in inter-service latency",
"day\": 2,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"Monitor average response time between services via distributed tracing (e.g., Jaeger, Zipkin) and compare to baseline",
"action_threshold\": \"Latency increase >50% for any critical service-to-service call",
"signal\": \"Increased error rates in service-to-service calls",
"day\": 5,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"Track HTTP 5xx/4xx rates and connection timeout errors via service mesh or API gateway logs",
"action_threshold\": \"Error rate >5% for any service dependency over 1-hour rolling window",
"signal\": \"Inconsistent financial data in read-after-write scenarios",
"day\": 8,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"Automated end-to-end tests that write financial transactions then immediately read them back",
"action_threshold\": \"Any test failure indicating data inconsistency",
"signal\": \"Distributed transaction rollback frequency",
"day\": 12,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"Monitor Saga/2PC transaction completion rates vs. rollbacks in transaction coordinator logs",
"action_threshold\": \"Rollback rate >10% of total distributed transactions",
"signal\": \"Development team reporting inability to test locally",
"day\": 15,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"Track frequency of \"can't reproduce locally\" tickets and time spent on environment setup",
"action_threshold\": \">30% of developers reporting local testing issues in weekly survey",
"signal\": \"Deployment pipeline failures due to service dependencies",
"day\": 20,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"Monitor CI/CD pipeline failures specifically related to service version mismatches or dependency errors",
"action_threshold\": \">20% of deployments blocked by dependency issues",
"signal\": \"Increased memory/CPU usage in API gateway",
"day\": 25,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"Infrastructure monitoring of gateway resource utilization and connection pool exhaustion",
"action_threshold\": \"Sustained >80% resource utilization for 1+ hours",
"signal\": \"Business logic errors from service boundary mismatches",
"day\": 28,\n            \"how_to_detect\": \"User-reported bugs where data flows correctly between services but produces wrong business outcomes",
"action_threshold\": \"Any production bug traceable to service boundary design flaw"
]

Redesign the solution to be robust against these failure modes. Add specific safeguards, checkpoints, and rollback mechanisms.

Output JSON: {"hardened_solution": "<redesigned approach>", "safeguards": ["<specific safeguard>"], "checkpoints": [{"milestone": "<m>", "go_nogo_criterion": "<criterion>"}], "rollback_plan": "<what to do if failing>"}
